description: A complete synthesizer voice: two oscillators, a state variable filter, a mixer, two envelopes, an LFO and a VCA, normalled together so a CV and a gate make sound, with every stage on its own jack

params.text: Tunes VCO 1 coarsely, two octaves up and two octaves down from the pitch at its CV input
Sets how deeply VCO 1 is modulated: turned left the modulation moves its frequency, turned right it moves its pulse width, and at the centre neither
Picks what modulates VCO 1, ENV 1 or the LFO; a cable in the MOD SRC jack on its row overrides this switch
Sets the width of VCO 1's pulse wave, from a thin spike at one end to a full square at the other
Hard syncs VCO 2 to VCO 1, restarting VCO 2's wave every time VCO 1's begins
Tunes VCO 2 coarsely, two octaves up and two octaves down from the pitch at its CV input
Sets how deeply VCO 2 is modulated: turned left the modulation moves its frequency, turned right it moves its pulse width, and at the centre neither
Picks what modulates VCO 2, ENV 2 or the LFO; a cable in the MOD SRC jack on its row overrides this switch
Sets the width of VCO 2's pulse wave, from a thin spike at one end to a full square at the other
Sets the cutoff of the filter
Sets the resonance of the filter, which self-oscillates at the top of its travel
Sets how deeply the cutoff is modulated, one direction from the centre adding and the other subtracting
Sweeps the response of the main filter output from lowpass, through notch, to highpass
Picks what modulates the cutoff, ENV 2 or the LFO; a cable in the MOD SRC jack on the VCF row overrides this switch
Picks which filter response feeds the VCA, the LP / HP output or the bandpass
Crossfades VCO 1 into the mix, its saw wave at one end and its pulse wave at the other, with the oscillator silent at the centre
Crossfades VCO 2 into the mix, its saw wave at one end and its pulse wave at the other, with the oscillator silent at the centre
Crossfades between the two external inputs, EXT 1 at one end and EXT 2 at the other; unpatched those are the internal noise and a 440Hz tuning tone
Turned on, the cutoff follows the main CV, so the filter tracks the pitch of the notes
Sets how long ENV 1 takes to rise to full
Sets how long ENV 1 takes to fall from full to the sustain level
Sets the level ENV 1 holds while its gate stays high
Sets the speed of the LFO
Picks what controls the VCA: ENV 1, or the voltage at the VEL/EXT input
Sets how long ENV 2 takes to rise to full
Sets how long ENV 2 takes to fall from full to the sustain level
Sets the level ENV 2 holds while its gate stays high

inputs.text: Sets the pitch of VCO 1, a volt per octave; unpatched it reads the main CV input, so both oscillators track the keyboard unless they are patched apart
Modulates VCO 1 in place of whatever the MOD SRC switch on its row picks
Sets the pitch of VCO 2, a volt per octave; unpatched it reads the main CV input
Modulates VCO 2 in place of whatever the MOD SRC switch on its row picks
Moves the filter cutoff, a volt per octave
Modulates the cutoff in place of whatever the MOD SRC switch on the VCF row picks
An external signal into the EXT 1 / EXT 2 crossfade; unpatched it reads the internal noise generator
An external signal into the EXT 1 / EXT 2 crossfade; unpatched it reads a 440Hz tuning tone
A trigger here restarts the LFO at the start of its cycle
Scales ENV 1, which is the usual way of applying velocity; with the VCA switch set to EXT it controls the VCA outright. Unpatched it reads as full
The gate that runs ENV 1; unpatched it reads the main gate input
The gate that runs ENV 2; unpatched it reads the main gate input
The main pitch input, a volt per octave, normalled to both oscillators; its channel count is one of those that set how many voices play
The main gate, normalled to both envelope gates

outputs.text: VCO 1's sawtooth wave on its own, before the mixer
VCO 1's pulse wave on its own, before the mixer
VCO 2's sawtooth wave on its own, before the mixer
VCO 2's pulse wave on its own, before the mixer
The filter's main response, swept from lowpass through notch to highpass by the LP / HP knob
The filter's bandpass response, which the LP / HP knob does not affect
The audio output of the voice, after the mixer, the filter and the VCA

notes: every jack takes polyphony, and the voice count is the widest channel count across the two oscillator CV jacks, the VCF CV jack, the two gate jacks and the main CV and gate jacks
a monophonic cable in any jack is read by every voice
the filter produces lowpass, notch, highpass and bandpass at once, and the TYPE switch only sets which of them reaches the VCA
